stop_condition: Every claim the candidate ships (code comments, printed installer/doctor text, README/CHANGELOG, test names and messages, CI comments, commit message) is TRUE at 1ea00bb, and no shipped behaviour contradicts what the candidate says it does. Findings that only make a true claim more precise are filed as v5.0.1, not fixed now.

findings.location: install.sh:554-556 (and install.ps1:444); false claims at README.md:300-302, README.md:363-364, CHANGELOG.md:174-178, and the commit message
findings.evidence: MEASURED, with a control, host bd hashed before and after (86e81a32... unchanged throughout). The new floor refusal is at install.sh:595 and exits at :654, but the --skip-beads-upgrade early-return sits ABOVE it at :554-556, so the flag returns before the refusal is ever reached. install.ps1 has the identical ordering: `if ($SkipBeadsUpgrade) { return }` at :444, refusal at :462. RUN A (control, no flag), fake bd reporting 0.47.1 on PATH: the refusal fires, `.claude/` is NOT created -- the candidate's claim holds on the default path. RUN B, same fake bd, `bash install.sh --skip-beads-upgrade <target>`: grep -c 'REFUSING to install' = 0, rc=3, and `find <target> -type f | wc -l` = 6965 -- a complete v5 install written onto bd 0.47.1, ending in the installer's own '[RED] VERIFICATION FAILED -- this install does not work yet (exit 3). Every file was written; 1 functional check(s) did not pass.' RUN C, environment form `CWP_SKIP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1` with no flag: identical -- 0 refusals, rc=3, 6965 files. So four shipped claims are false as written: README.md:300-302 'on an older bd it REFUSES before writing anything and prints the upgrade procedure'; README.md:363-364 '>= 1.1.2, the floor the installer enforces' (the enforced hard floor is MIN_BD_VERSION=0.47 at install.sh:74, unchanged by this candidate); CHANGELOG.md:176 'On an older bd, `install.sh` REFUSES, exit 1, before writing anything (verified by execution), and so does `install.ps1`'; and the commit message's 'The installer now refuses every bd below 1.1.2, so a 0.47.x teammate who trusted it would be refused.' This is also the stop rule's second blocking clause -- shipped behaviour contradicting what the candidate says it does -- because install.sh:596-600 states the refusal's own purpose as: 'Returning here would let the install proceed and write v5 over a working v4.1 into a bd configuration v5 does not support -- the post-install doctor would then fail, which is warning where the installer should refuse (the claude-workflow-plugin-q5l6 lesson).' RUN B and RUN C are exactly that outcome. The candidate introduced the inconsistency: at 32b12b2 the documented floor WAS 0.47 and --skip-beads-upgrade proceeding on 0.47.x was consistent with the contract; this candidate raised the documented floor to 1.1.2 on one path only. Aggravating, and not covered by any assertion: the flag's own printed help (install.sh --help, lines 36-42 of its output) still reads 'Do NOT offer to upgrade a bd older than the recommended version. The install still proceeds (the hard floor is 0.47 and every bd call is version-tolerant)' -- it promises to suppress an OFFER that no longer exists, never says it now suppresses a REFUSAL, and asserts a floor README and CHANGELOG contradict; install.ps1:90-91 and :106-108 carry the PowerShell twin ('the hard floor is 0.47', 'an older bd is degraded, not broken'). The persistent env form means the population most likely to carry CWP_SKIP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1 into v5 is precisely the population that set it to escape the unpinned auto-upgrade this candidate removes. installer-flags section 9 does not cover the flag; the only coverage is the untouched L2 spec .claude/tests/component/specs/installer-beads-upgrade.sh:284-285, which still asserts '--skip-beads-upgrade opts out entirely'.
findings.description: The documented --skip-beads-upgrade flag and its CWP_SKIP_BEADS_UPGRADE=1 environment form silently bypass the v5 bd floor refusal in BOTH installers, writing a full v5 install onto a below-floor bd. README, CHANGELOG and the commit message state the refusal unconditionally, so all three are false as written, and the resulting behaviour is the exact 'warning where the installer should refuse' failure the refusal says it exists to prevent. Either the refusal must move above the skip early-return in both installers, or every surface that states it (README, CHANGELOG, both installers' help text, the commit message) must say which invocations it does not cover -- and the installer-flags section 9 battery needs a leg for whichever is chosen, since nothing in L1 exercises the flag today.

findings.evidence: The comment reads: 'A CI lane that installs bd 1.1.2 from a pinned, sha256-verified tarball -- with no second bd downloaded anywhere in the job, verified by grepping the whole job log -- was measured reporting "installed bd 1.3.1".' The parenthetical asserts the absence as FACT and offers the grep as VERIFICATION of it. The candidate's own commit message calls that claim disproved: 'its floor-row paragraph said "no second bd is downloaded anywhere in the job", which the diagnosis disproved.' The diagnosis is that a second bd WAS downloaded in the job -- installer-flags.test.sh drove install.sh into its upgrade arm, which ran an unpinned `curl ... | bash` that fetched and installed whatever beads released last over /usr/local/bin/bd (measured in the commit message and in installer-flags.test.sh:63-75 as sha256 1db3b1b5... -> 21351856..., version 1.3.1). ATTRIBUTION, verified: `git log -S 'no second bd downloaded anywhere' -- .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh` returns ed9ea91, which is inside this change set (the diff under review is 32b12b2..1ea00bb and spans ed9ea91 + 1ea00bb); `git grep -i 'second bd' 32b12b2` returns NOTHING anywhere in the tree, so this text is new in this change set, not inherited. Unlike the two sibling sites, this comment never self-corrects: the remaining ten lines are about naming the binary, and nothing in the block mentions the installer, the upgrade arm or the curl. A maintainer reading it comes away with precisely the false premise that the commit message says cost '45-minute CI rounds'. CONTRAST, which is why the other two sites are not this finding: .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh:1366 is correctly scoped -- 'grepping the entire job log showed NO second bd downloaded anywhere' is a true statement about what the grep SHOWED, used to explain why the question could not be settled; and .github/workflows/test.yml:229 states it as fact but is corrected eight lines later by its own 'THE AGENT' paragraph. CORROBORATION: this candidate ships, in the same commit, a new LESSONS.md entry that names this exact defect -- 'AN EMPTY GREP IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE UNTIL THE GREP ITSELF IS SHOWN TO WORK. This is the absence-reads-as-success family caught inside my own verification rather than in shipped code.' The grep here was never shown to work, and could not have: a `curl | bash` inside a captured test subshell emits no line the job-log grep was looking for.
findings.description: A shipped code comment in workflow-doctor.sh asserts, as grep-verified fact, the one claim this candidate's own commit message identifies as disproved by its root-cause diagnosis. It is new text in this change set, it never self-corrects, and it is a textbook instance of the empty-grep lesson the same commit adds to LESSONS.md.

findings.evidence: The header comment for the Beads upgrader section (install.sh:512-536) ends: 'Non-fatal throughout: the hard floor is still MIN_BD_VERSION, so every exit path here continues the install.' That section contains upgrade_beads_if_old, into which this candidate added a refusal that terminates the process at install.sh:654 (`exit 1`, inside the guard opened at :595). So 'every exit path here continues the install' is false at 1ea00bb. `git blame -L 535,536 1ea00bb -- install.sh` attributes the comment to fdfd6ce (2026-08-03), and the diff hunks confirm the lines are untouched context -- `git diff 32b12b2 1ea00bb -- install.sh | grep 'Non-fatal'` returns nothing -- so the candidate did not write the sentence but did falsify it. It is not merely stale: it accurately states the OLD design (advisory upgrader, hard floor 0.47) that R5-F1 shows was only half-changed, so it is the same incomplete edit showing up in a second place.
findings.description: A shipped code comment in install.sh states that every exit path in the Beads-upgrader section continues the install. This candidate added an exit 1 to that section, making the sentence false. It is untouched context, but the candidate is what falsified it.

findings.location: commit message of 1ea00bbe60db52d6cdf8786f7695c2df63b1ecba, the RELEASE TEXT bullet about README's bd:schema table
findings.evidence: The bullet reads: 'README's bd:schema table omitted the new 1.3.1:66 member and still called 1.3.0 "the CI ceiling"; its floor-row paragraph said "no second bd is downloaded anywhere in the job", which the diagnosis disproved.' The first two conjuncts are TRUE -- verified at `git show 32b12b2:README.md`, whose table carries four rows ending '| 1.3.0 | 66 | validated -- the CI ceiling (`l1-doctor-bd-max`) and the development host |' and no 1.3.1 row. The third is FALSE. README had no floor-row paragraph at 32b12b2 at all: the floor row was a single table cell, '| 1.1.2 | 53 | validated -- the CI floor (`l1-unit`, every run) |', and the explanatory paragraph beginning '**Why the floor row says UNCONFIRMED**' is NEW in this candidate, added already in corrected form. The quoted phrase was never in README in any commit: `git grep -i 'second bd' 32b12b2` returns nothing tree-wide, `git show ed9ea91:README.md | grep -i 'second bd'` returns nothing, and `git log -S 'no second bd' -- README.md` returns no commits. This is not a cosmetic misattribution -- it is the proximate cause of R5-F2 surviving: the correction was aimed at a file that never carried the phrase, while the three files that do carry it (workflow-doctor.sh:1474, workflow-doctor.test.sh:1366, test.yml:229) were all introduced by this same change set and went unreviewed for it.
findings.description: The commit message claims to have corrected a disproved phrase in README's floor-row paragraph. README never contained that phrase, and had no floor-row paragraph before this candidate. The real carriers were added by this change set and left uncorrected, so the false bullet is what hid R5-F2.

findings.evidence: v5.0.1. The SUPERSEDED-then-RESOLVED paragraph states as fact '-- and no second bd downloaded in the job. The pinned binary was being overwritten mid-suite.' Eight lines later the same paragraph names the agent: 'install.sh then ran its beads upgrade -- an UNPINNED `curl ... | bash` that installs whatever beads released last -- over this job's pinned binary', which is a second bd being downloaded in the job. The two sentences contradict each other, but a reader of the whole paragraph reaches the true one, so this makes a true account imprecise rather than leaving a false belief standing. Distinguished from R5-F2 on exactly that ground: workflow-doctor.sh:1474 never self-corrects.
findings.description: test.yml states the disproved 'no second bd downloaded in the job' as fact, then contradicts it eight lines later in the same comment block. Worth tightening to 'none was LOGGED' so the narration matches the resolution it introduces, but the paragraph as a whole conveys the truth.

findings.evidence: v5.0.1. README says the installer 'REFUSES before writing anything'. `mkdir -p "$TARGET"` runs at install.sh:454, before upgrade_beads_if_old is called at :762, so on a target path that does not yet exist the installer creates an empty directory and then refuses. install.sh's own refusal text is more careful and is TRUE as written -- 'Nothing has been written. Your existing install is untouched.' -- and the substantive claim is asserted by installer-flags 9.3 ('NOTHING was written into the target (no .claude/)'), which measured no on RUN A. install.sh:600-602 already discloses the mkdir honestly in its own comment. Precision only; no plugin file is written and no existing install is touched.
findings.description: README's 'REFUSES before writing anything' is a slight overstatement: an empty target directory is created at install.sh:454 before the refusal. The installer's own printed wording is already accurate; only the README phrasing overreaches.
